The main urban centers of the religion are [[Sahneh]], [[Kerend-e Gharb]], and [[Gahvareh]], and other important cities include [[Kermanshah]], [[Sarpol-e Zahab]] and [[Qasr-e Shirin]].{{sfnp|Hamzeh'ee|1990|p=39}}
The main urban centers of the religion are [[Sahneh]], [[Kerend-e Gharb]], and [[Gahvareh]], and other important cities include [[Kermanshah]], [[Sarpol-e Zahab]] and [[Qasr-e Shirin]].{{sfnp|Hamzeh'ee|1990|p=39}}


Other areas in Iran with a significant Yarsan population include [[Hashtgerd]] and [[Varamin]], near [[Tehran]], and [[Maragheh]] and [[Tabriz]] in [[Azerbaijan (Iran)|Iranian Azerbaijan]],{{sfnp|Hamzeh'ee|1990|p=39}} where important Turkic-speaking Yarsan communities live and use [[Turkic languages|Turkic]] for many of their religious texts. The Yarsani tradition claims that all early communities used [[Gorani language|Gorani]] as their religious language, but that over time, some groups were forced to adopt a Turkic language closely akin to [[Azerbaijani language|Azeri]] for all purposes, including religion.{{sfnp|Kreyenbroek|Kanakis|2020|pp=32–33}}
Yarsani adherents in Lorestan province included the Lak tribes of Nurali, Chavari, Mirbeg, Tarhan, and part of the Owlad Qobad in the counties of Delfan and [[Kuhdasht County|Kuhdasht]].<ref>سجادی، علی. "تحلیل بازتاب رفتارهای آئینی اهل ‌حق در میراث مادی بر اساس کاوش‌های باستان‌شناسی، مطالعات اسنادی و باستان /مردم‌‌شناسی"، نامه انسان‌شناسی، 18، 32، 1400، pp. 187.</ref> Other areas in Iran with a significant Yarsan population include [[Hashtgerd]] and [[Varamin]], near [[Tehran]], and [[Maragheh]] and [[Tabriz]] in [[Azerbaijan (Iran)|Iranian Azerbaijan]],{{sfnp|Hamzeh'ee|1990|p=39}} where important Turkic-speaking Yarsan communities live and use [[Turkic languages|Turkic]] for many of their religious texts. The Yarsani tradition claims that all early communities used [[Gorani language|Gorani]] as their religious language, but that over time, some groups were forced to adopt a Turkic language closely akin to [[Azerbaijani language|Azeri]] for all purposes, including religion.{{sfnp|Kreyenbroek|Kanakis|2020|pp=32–33}}


In Iraq, Yarsan followers mainly live in [[Mosul]], [[Kirkuk]], [[Kalar, Iraq|Kalar]], [[Khanaqin]], [[Erbil]], [[Sulaymaniyah]], and [[Halabja]].{{sfnp|Hamzeh'ee|1990|p=39}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kaka'is - The men with big moustaches ‌|website=Pukmedia |url=https://www.pukmedia.com/EN/Details/71230 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221104081419/https://www.pukmedia.com/EN/Details/71230 |archive-date=2022-11-04 |access-date=2022-04-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017 |title=Kaka'i in Iraq |website=Minority Rights Group |url=https://minorityrights.org/communities/kakai/ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=Apr 23, 2021 |title=Iraq's Kaka'i minority aspires to be represented in political process |website=North Press Agency |url=https://npasyria.com/en/58142/ }}</ref>
